# openapi-contract

Validate complete PSR-7 request/response exchanges against OpenAPI 3.0/3.1
contracts. Framework-neutral; fail-closed on anything outside the support
matrix.

Install:

```bash
composer require rasuvaeff/openapi-contract
```

Rules:
- unsupported OpenAPI versions (`UnsupportedVersion`), dialects, remote
  references, ambiguous templates, malformed shapes (`InvalidContract`), and
  parameter `content`/unsupported styles (`UnsupportedSerialization`) fail
  closed at load time; so does every Schema Object the validators will read
  (parameters, request/response media types, response and multipart part
  headers): each is compiled by the factory in its own direction, and an
  unsupported assertion keyword, a foreign `$schema`, a 3.0 numeric
  `exclusiveMinimum` or an unparsable `pattern` at any depth is
  `InvalidContract` from `fromArray()`/`fromJson()`/`fromFile()`, never from
  `validate*()`;
- every exception implements `ContractException`: `InvalidContract` (base of
  `UnsupportedVersion`/`UnsupportedSerialization`), `InvalidLimits`,
  `UnknownOperation`, `ContractViolation`; the concrete parents stay
  `\InvalidArgumentException` and `\RuntimeException`;
- `fromFile()` resolves relative `$ref`s to sibling JSON/YAML files inside
  the entry file's directory tree; absolute paths, URI schemes,
  percent-encoded paths, traversal, and symlink escapes are rejected before
  reading, while `fromArray()`/`fromJson()` accept same-document refs only;
- Path Item and Operation `parameters` merge by location and name, the
  Operation's declaration replacing the Path Item's; the same pair declared
  twice inside ONE list is `InvalidContract` (header names compare
  case-insensitively);
- a request URI without an authority is matched by path alone: a relative
  server and a host-agnostic request are not rejected for failing to name a
  host the request never claimed;
- a `pattern` from the document runs in the backend's `preg_match`; a contract
  is a trusted input, and PHP's `pcre.backtrack_limit` bounds each match
  fail-closed rather than hanging;
- a header parameter named `Accept`, `Content-Type` or `Authorization` is
  ignored (both specifications say so), and under OAS 3.0 a `requestBody` on
  GET/HEAD/DELETE is ignored too — 3.1 permits it and validates it;
- each path-template placeholder requires an effective same-named `in: path`
  parameter with explicit `required: true`; extra path parameters fail at
  contract compilation;
- declarations are read strictly: a `requestBody`, `parameters`, `content`,
  `encoding`, `headers` or Schema Object in a shape this package cannot read
  is `InvalidContract` at load time (never a silently unchecked part of the
  contract), a boolean field written as a string is rejected instead of
  falling back to its default, a schema carrying `.nan`/`.inf` is rejected
  before reaching the backend, a document whose `paths` yield no operation is
  rejected, and an unparsable YAML file is `InvalidContract`, not the parser's
  own exception;
- `$ref` is resolved only where it is a keyword: never inside `example`, an
  Example Object's `value`, a Schema Object's `default`/`const`/`enum`, or a
  specification extension — those hold the author's data and are kept as
  written (an Example Object reached through `$ref` still resolves);
- `$ref` siblings follow the declared dialect: 3.0 ignores them everywhere;
  3.1 keeps `summary`/`description` on a Reference Object (overriding the
  referenced ones) and applies a Schema Object's siblings in addition to the
  reference, compiling `{$ref: X, maximum: 10}` to the matching `allOf`;
- OpenAPI 3.0 and 3.1 use separate schema compilation paths (3.0 `nullable`
  and boolean exclusive bounds are normalized; 3.1 rides the 2020-12 base
  dialect);
- documents are bounded: byte size, JSON depth, `$ref` depth, node budget,
  plus graph-wide file-count and byte budgets for multi-file documents;
- response selection order is exact status, then `NXX` range, then `default`;
  an unknown status never cascades into invented body/header violations;
- body validation reads seekable streams from the beginning and restores the
  original position in `finally`; non-seekable bodies are never consumed and
  yield `request.body.non_seekable` / `response.body.non_seekable` when their
  declared content needs validation;
- `Limits::$messageBodyBytes` defaults to 1 MiB; larger bodies yield
  `request.body.too_large` / `response.body.too_large` without entering
  schema validation or diagnostics; a JSON body nested deeper than 64 levels
  yields `request.body.json` / `response.body.json` (not configurable);
- `readOnly`/`writeOnly` properties apply directionally: a `readOnly`
  property is NOT REQUIRED on a request and a `writeOnly` one NOT REQUIRED on
  a response — the `required` entry is dropped, the subschema is kept, so the
  property stays declared and typed (a closed object still admits it, an open
  one still checks its type); recursive through `properties`, `items`,
  `additionalProperties`, `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf`, never into `not`;
  `SchemaCheck::effective($schema, $direction)` returns exactly that rewrite;
- declared `security` is NOT enforced: requirements compile and are checked
  for referencing a declared scheme, but a request missing its credential
  validates clean — authorization is the application's middleware, not this
  package;
- `allowReserved` is compiled and exposed on the parameter, never read by
  validation (after parsing, an encoded reserved character cannot be told from
  an unencoded one) — it is a hand-off to consumers that render query values,
  which cannot derive it from the schema;
- budgets are `Limits`, not constants: `new Limits(documentBytes:,
  messageBodyBytes:, documentFiles:, documentNodes:)` passed to any factory; a
  budget below 1 throws `InvalidLimits` (an `\InvalidArgumentException`
  implementing `ContractException`). `documentNodes` bounds
  what a document expands into, which for YAML anchors is unrelated to what it
  weighs. `*.body.too_large` means the validator
  declined to read that body, NOT that the message is invalid — raise the
  budget rather than treating it as a failed verdict;
- `Operation` is a read model: nothing public validates a hand-built
  operation, but the constructor is `@api` and append-only (a minor may add a
  defaulted parameter at the end) — construct it with named arguments; the
  `CompiledParameter`, `CompiledRequestBody` and `CompiledResponses` shapes
  are read-only for consumers — minor releases may add keys to them;
- `CompiledRequestBody`/`CompiledResponses` (`@psalm-type` on `Operation`)
  are the resolved Request Body Object / Responses Object: `$ref`s on the way
  to a schema resolved, `required` boolean, `content` keyed by media type,
  `encoding`/`headers` keyed by name, every `schema` a boolean or a keyword
  map (`{}` = unconstrained), other keys kept as written; responses keyed by
  status as PHP reads it (`"200"` → `int 200`), `NXX`, or `default`;
- a response header declaring the boolean schema `false` fails closed when the
  header is present, as a body declaring it does;
- root `security` is inherited by operations; explicit `security: []` marks
  an operation anonymous; credentials live in the generator package;
- `components.securitySchemes` compile into a typed map: a scheme without a
  supported `type` (`apiKey`, `http`, `mutualTLS` on 3.1 only, `oauth2`,
  `openIdConnect`) or missing a field its type requires fails closed; an
  `oauth2` scheme with an empty `flows` object compiles to empty `flows`, and
  URL fields are checked as non-empty strings, not parsed as URLs;
- a present response header with a `schema` is decoded `simple`-style and
  validated (`response.header.schema` / `response.header.serialization`);
  `content`-form or non-`simple` declarations fail closed as
  `response.header.unsupported`; a `Content-Type` declaration is ignored;
- `format` is asserted where the backend checks it and an annotation
  elsewhere (never rejects): asserted on strings — `date`, `time`,
  `date-time`, `duration`, `uri`, `uri-reference`, `uri-template`, `regex`,
  `ipv4`, `ipv6`, `uuid`, `email`, `hostname`, `idn-hostname`, `idn-email`,
  `iri`, `iri-reference`, `json-pointer`, `relative-json-pointer`; on
  integers — `int32` (−2³¹…2³¹−1), `int64` (−2⁶³…2⁶³−1); annotation only —
  `byte`, `binary`, `password`, `float`, `double`, anything unknown. Asserting
  string formats is a pinned divergence from league/openapi-psr7-validator;
- accepted and never read (no verdict depends on them): `allowEmptyValue`,
  `discriminator`, `xml`, `externalDocs`, `deprecated`;
- `ext-bcmath` is optional: with it `multipleOf` is evaluated in decimal
  arithmetic, without it in floating point with a `1e-14` tolerance;
- three pinned divergences from the specification: a percent-encoded `|` or
  space inside a `pipeDelimited`/`spaceDelimited` value is folded into the
  delimiter (as PHP's own query parsing does, so `?ids=a%7Cb` is two elements
  here and one per the spec — a value containing the delimiter cannot be
  expressed); a Header Object carrying `name`/`in` is ignored rather than
  refused; `example` and `examples` together are both kept instead of being
  refused as mutually exclusive. `deepObject` is NOT one of them —
  `f%5Ba%5D=1` and `f[a]=1` agree with PHP;
- multi-file resolution is differentially tested against cebe/php-openapi
  (dev-only oracle, OAS 3.0): pinned divergences are the depth budget on
  deep `$ref` chains and fast rejection of cross-file cycles.

API reference:
- `Contract::fromArray(array $document, ?Limits $limits = null): Contract` /
  `fromJson(string $json, string $source = 'openapi.json', ?Limits $limits = null)` /
  `fromFile(string $path, ?Limits $limits = null)` (YAML via suggested
  symfony/yaml; multi-file relative `$ref`s under the entry directory) build
  the immutable compiled contract.
- `Limits` (readonly): `documentBytes` (default 10 MiB),
  `messageBodyBytes` (default 1 MiB), `documentFiles` (default 64),
  `documentNodes` (default 5 000 000), with `Limits::DEFAULT_DOCUMENT_BYTES` /
  `DEFAULT_MESSAGE_BODY_BYTES` / `DEFAULT_DOCUMENT_FILES` /
  `DEFAULT_DOCUMENT_NODES` as the constants behind them.
- `Contract::operations(): list<Operation>`;
  `Contract::operation(string $key): Operation` throws `UnknownOperation`.
- `Contract::securitySchemes(): array<string, CompiledSecurityScheme>` —
  `components.securitySchemes` keyed by the names `Operation::$security`
  refers to; each entry is `type` plus exactly the fields its type defines
  (`apiKey`: `name`, `in`; `http`: `scheme`, `bearerFormat?`; `oauth2`:
  `flows` → per declared flow `authorizationUrl?`/`tokenUrl?`/`refreshUrl?`
  and `scopes`; `openIdConnect`: `openIdConnectUrl`; `mutualTLS`: nothing);
  descriptions and extensions are dropped.
- `Operation` (readonly): `key` (operationId or `METHOD /path` fallback),
  `operationId`, `method`, `path`, `parameters` (compiled list with name/in/
  required/style/explode/allowReserved/schema/specPointer — the last being the
  JSON Pointer of the declaration itself, which for a Path Item's parameters is
  not under the operation — plus `example`/`examples` keys
  present exactly when the document declares them — annotations for
  validation, inputs for the generator's example phase), `requestBody`,
  `requestBody` (`CompiledRequestBody`), `responses` (`CompiledResponses`),
  `security`, `servers` (full model: scheme/host/port/base, operation > path
  > root precedence, variable defaults substituted; undeclared variables,
  non-enum defaults, unsupported schemes, and userinfo/query/fragment fail
  closed at compile time; read a base path as `$servers[$i]['base']`),
  `dialect`.
- `Contract::match(RequestInterface): ?MatchedOperation` — method, server
  base paths, concrete-before-templated precedence, split on the raw `/`
  then a single percent-decode per segment (`/pets/a%2Fb` matches
  `/pets/{name}` with `name = "a/b"`; `/a%2Fb/x` does not match `/a/b/x`),
  placeholders that share a segment with literals (`/report.{format}`, `/{a}-{b}`); an absolute server additionally
  requires the normalized scheme/host/effective-port the request URI carries
  (path-only requests and relative servers stay host-agnostic); a declared
  path whose server authority disagrees validates as
  `request.server.mismatch`, not `request.operation.unknown`;
  `requireMatch()` throws `UnknownOperation`.
- `MatchedOperation` (readonly): `operation`, `pathParameters`
  (raw, undecoded).
- `Contract::validateRequest(RequestInterface): ValidationResult` —
  parameters per location (style/explode deserialization, schema), JSON
  request bodies (syntax separately from schema).
- Percent-decoding happens where an encoding exists: path, query (`+` is a
  space, it is form-encoded content) and cookie. A cookie string is split on
  `;` (plus optional whitespace), never on `&`, which is a cookie-octet:
  `sid=abc&def` is one seven-character value. A header value — request or
  response — is read VERBATIM: `%20` stays three characters. A header value
  therefore cannot carry its own style delimiter.
- A wire string becomes an `integer`/`number` only by the JSON number grammar
  (`-?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)?([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, anchored): `.5`, `5.`,
  ` 5`, `5\n`, `+5`, `0x1A` stay strings and fail the schema; an integer past
  PHP's range is a float of the same magnitude, not a saturated int.
- `Contract::validateExchange(Request, Response): ValidationResult` — both
  sides: request violations plus response status selection, response
  headers (required presence, `simple`-style value decoding and schema in
  the response direction), media types (`application/json` and `*+json`),
  body schema.
- `Operation::responseFor(int $status): ?array` — the Response Object a
  status resolves to (`['key' => ..., 'definition' => ...]`), by the same
  exact/`NXX`/`default` selection response validation uses; `null` when the
  status is undeclared or is not an HTTP status at all;
- `Contract::validateResponse(string $operationKey, Response): ValidationResult`
  — validates a response fixture without a request; unknown keys yield one
  `response.operation.unknown` violation. Response selection remains exact,
  then `NXX`, then `default`.
- a parameter name occurring more than once where its style admits one value
  is `request.parameter.duplicate`, not a value: which occurrence the
  application reads is a property of the runtime (PHP last, Go first, Node
  both). Exploded lists are unaffected;
- a `content` map is matched by specificity, not by key order: exact
  `type/subtype` > `type/*+suffix` > `type/*` > `*/*`, and only equally
  specific keys are settled by declaration order;
- Request body media types: JSON, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` using
  form parameter semantics, and bounded `multipart/form-data` with JSON/binary
  parts, arrays, and per-property encoding content types and headers. An
  `encoding.contentType` on a form or multipart property carries a whole
  document: JSON is decoded and validated against the property schema, any
  other media type is validated as the string it already is. A declared part
  header must be present when `required` and must satisfy its schema, read with
  the `simple` style. Default part content type: `text/plain` (primitives),
  `application/octet-stream` (binary), `application/json` (objects), and for
  arrays the item type's default. Malformed body serialization fails as
  `request.body.decode`.
- A response declaring a schema that arrives with an empty body →
  `response.body.missing`, the mirror of `request.body.missing`. Excluded:
  `204`, `304`, every response to `HEAD`, and a media type entry with no schema
  or the unconstrained boolean one.
- Declared non-JSON media types (request or response): no schema → opaque,
  valid; string-typed schema → the raw payload is validated as that string
  (`*.body.schema`); any other schema → `request.body.unsupported` /
  `response.body.unsupported`. Undeclared media types → `*.body.media_type`.
- `ValidationResult` (readonly): `violations` (`list<Violation>`),
  `isValid(): bool`, `assertValid(): void` throws `ContractViolation`.
- `ValidationResultFormatter::format(ValidationResult): string` renders every
  violation in stable order with bounded fields/values/depth/items. A body
  `actual` and a cookie `actual` are redacted wholesale; another parameter's `actual` is rendered with members
  whose name matches `authorization|api[-_]?key|token|secret|password|cookie`
  replaced, and is redacted outright when the instance path itself matches.
- Schema compilation is cached per `Contract` / `SchemaCheck` instance,
  keyed by schema, direction and dialect; the cache never evicts, so hold one
  instance per document. A hand-passed schema may `$ref` only inside itself
  (`#/$defs/…`); any other target, a schema that cannot be JSON-encoded
  (`NAN`, malformed UTF-8, >512 levels) or a list in place of an object
  raises `InvalidContract`.
- `Contract::accepts(mixed $value, array $schema, SchemaDirection $direction = SchemaDirection::Request): bool`
  runs that same check on one Schema Object, binding the document's dialect
  and reusing the cache. `SchemaCheck::accepts($value, $schema, SchemaDialect
  $dialect, SchemaDirection $direction = Request)` is the same check for a
  consumer holding an `Operation` and no contract.
- `SchemaCheck::effective(array $schema, SchemaDirection $direction): array`
  — the directional rewrite the validators apply before judging a value
  (`required` entries of foreign properties dropped, subschemas kept,
  recursive, `not` untouched, dialect-independent, idempotent), for a
  consumer that generates values for one direction.
- `SchemaDirection` (enum): `Request`, `Response`. Decides which properties
  are required — a `readOnly` one is not required on a request, a `writeOnly`
  one not on a response; both stay declared and typed.
- `SchemaDialect` (enum): `OpenApi30`, `OpenApi31`. `Operation::$dialect`
  carries the document's, filled by compilation; a hand-built `Operation`
  defaults to `OpenApi31`. A schema the dialect cannot read raises
  `InvalidContract`.
- Values are judged as `json_decode()` produces them: a JSON object is a
  `stdClass`, not an associative array. Decode a parameter's wire string
  before checking it.
- `Violation` (readonly): `code` (stable, e.g. `request.parameter.missing`,
  `response.body.schema`), `operation`, `location`, `instancePath`,
  `specPointer` (JSON Pointer into the document), `expected`, `actual`
  (bounded), `message`.
- Violation codes (complete set; the code is the stable contract, the
  formatter's message text is a diagnostic that may be reworded):
  `request.operation.unknown`, `request.server.mismatch`,
  `request.parameter.duplicate`, `request.parameter.missing`,
  `request.parameter.serialization`,
  `request.parameter.schema`, `request.body.missing`,
  `request.body.media_type`, `request.body.json`, `request.body.decode`,
  `request.body.schema`, `request.body.unsupported`, `request.body.too_large`,
  `request.body.non_seekable`, `request.body.unreadable`,
  `response.operation.unknown`, `response.status.invalid`,
  `response.status.mismatch`, `response.header.missing`,
  `response.header.serialization`, `response.header.schema`,
  `response.header.unsupported`, `response.body.missing`,
  `response.body.media_type`, `response.body.json`, `response.body.schema`,
  `response.body.unsupported`, `response.body.too_large`,
  `response.body.non_seekable`, `response.body.unreadable`.
- `ContractViolation::fromResult(ValidationResult)` uses the complete bounded
  formatter output as the exception message.
- Exceptions: all implement `ContractException`; `InvalidContract` (base,
  extends `\InvalidArgumentException`), `UnsupportedVersion`,
  `UnsupportedSerialization`, `InvalidLimits` (extends
  `\InvalidArgumentException`, raised by `Limits` for a budget below 1),
  `UnknownOperation`, `ContractViolation` (extends `\RuntimeException`).

Example:

```php
use Rasuvaeff\OpenApiContract\Contract;

$contract = Contract::fromFile(__DIR__ . '/openapi.json');
$result = $contract->validateExchange($request, $response);
$result->assertValid();
```
